title: Lead sheets, iPads and the old days of mailing out music
summary: She carries few sheets now because Italian musicians use iPads and photos of music; both she and Rowe recall mailing packages and waiting for replies.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Okay. Now do you carry music with you, like lead sheets?

They usually write and ask me for a list in advance so that they can look over the music and I do carry a few sheets, not many. I used to carry much more but now we have of course all these little programs on the iPad and most musicians over there have those too.
So they can pull up — and then they can always take pictures of the music so I don’t have to bring copies for everyone.
It’s getting easier, yeah. Yeah I can recall those days of putting a letter in the mail with your package, or you’re sending things out to little record companies.
You’re waiting and waiting. And then I used to save a list, I called it my no folder, right? Thanks for your letter but no.
